_doc: Farhold knobs (round 4). Everything the game tunes lives here: the player's base numbers, how enemies scale and rank up, what drops, zones and their level bands, dungeons, chests, pets, light, how far you can see and how much the sky exaggerates. js/rpg.js reads player/enemies/ranks/loot; js/main.js reads world/terrain/sky/spawn/light; js/zones.js, js/dungeon.js, js/chests.js and js/pets.js read their own blocks.

player._boardDoc: Knee-deep. swimDepth is where you stop walking and start swimming; boardDepth is where you climb into the boat, and it is deliberately shallower. 'We should make it so you equip the raft even if your knees are in the water, not only when at the absolute river line, but up to the shore as well.' Read by js/player.js when deciding to board.
player._damageDoc: damagePerLevel is what a level is worth in raw damage. A weapon's base does not change when you level but an enemy's health compounds every level, so without this a perfect bow at level 20 could not scratch a level-25 anything. Round 14 moved it: the level term multiplies the WEAPON'S OWN DICE and damageFlat is added afterwards (js/rpg.js derive), so gear no longer dilutes the weapon — 0.10 -> 0.11 keeps the overall curve where the simulator tuned it.
player._regenDoc: Share of maximum health you get back each second while nothing is fighting you. Without it a character who walked out of a fight at a third health stayed there — hpRegen is zero without gear that grants it, and there is no potion in the starting kit.
player._arrowSplashDoc: Round 14: an arrow used to burst for 2.6 m at full power on every shot, for free, while a melee jab was 0.65 of a hit inside a 0.3 m splash. An arrow hits what you aimed at now; the quiver's arrowBurst affix is what turns it back into an area shot, which is what that affix is for.

combat._doc: What a hit feels like, round 14. The per-shape numbers — knockback, stagger, hit-stop, shake — live on the strike shapes in js/weapons.js, because a shape is where they belong. These are the few that are global. R19 — THIS BLOCK IS NOW READ: js/combat-feel.js tuneFeel() takes it at boot, and its COMBAT_FEEL holds the five spent in js/actors.js and js/player.js. Note hitStopMaxMs is milliseconds where the code keeps seconds.

ranged._doc: A bow's rate of fire used to be the light-melee swing clock, because `bow` was in neither weapon table and profileOf fell through to the `light` category: 1.91 shots a second with no draw, no nock and no reload, and nobody designed it. The per-base numbers are in js/weapons.js RANGED; these are the shared ones, and R19 — they are now READ: tuneWeapons() overwrites RANGED with them at boot, so editing them here moves the game.

staff._doc: A staff cast a free shaped area spell every 0.6 s with no cast time, no mana and no choice — the most powerful weapon in the game and the least interesting. It charges now: a tap is still free and weak, a full channel is 1.6x damage over twice the radius, and it drinks mana while it builds. R19 — THIS BLOCK IS NOW THE LIVE COPY: tuneWeapons() writes it into js/weapons.js STAFF_CHARGE at boot, which js/player.js and js/rpg.js hold by reference.

progression._doc: XP curve lives in js/rpg.js (xpForLevel), written in fractions of `levelCap` so a 100-level world is the same climb cut into twice as many steps. At cap 50: level 2 at 58 xp, level 10 at ~3,500, level 30 at ~30,400, level 50 at ~118,700. `levelCap` is set by the world screen and rewritten into this object at boot.

_xpDoc: R22 — WHERE EXPERIENCE COMES FROM, AND HOW MUCH. Every one of these is a multiplier on what the game paid before this round, and every XP award in the game goes through js/rpg.js `killXpFor` or `eventXp` so there is one place to change them. The report: 'Companions running around one-shotting everything... I was level 22 and teleported to a level 20-22 zone and after just a few kills from my companions I was level 30, 31. I reached level 30 in about 10 minutes.'

xp._doc: kill: a kill pays a fifth of what it used to ('cut XP gains from kills down to just 20% of the current value'). killFalloffPerLevel: each level the enemy is BELOW you takes this share off the award, so five levels below pays nothing at all ('anything 5 levels lower should not reward any xp'). killBonusPerLevelAbove/Cap: the other side of the same rule — something above your level is worth more, up to 60% more. quest/event/landmark: turn-ins, cleared places and the little 'experience for the walk' awards, which were 20-60 and are now 60-180 before the zone scaling. perZoneLevel: what a level of ZONE adds to an event award — it replaces five different per-PLAYER-level multipliers (0.15, 0.15, 0.1, 0.1, 0.12) that had grown up one at a time.

enemies._doc: Health and damage are SEPARATE curves. They used to share `perLevel`, which meant a five-level gap doubled an enemy's damage as well as its health and the fight stopped being winnable. A higher-level enemy should be much tougher and only somewhat harder hitting.

spawn._doc: Enemies appear in a ring around the player, out of sight, and are cleaned up when you walk far enough away. A spawn is usually a whole PACK rather than one body, and `js/encounters.js` turns some of them into a set piece — a warband on the march, a hunt, an ambush. Round 4 raised maxAlive from 14 to 38 and shortened the ring, because the old numbers left one straggler at a time wandering a very large map.

loot._affixDoc: How often each kind of property turns up. Emberveil's generator picks uniformly from 59 affixes, 40 of which are exotic conditionals — so a weapon almost never rolled plain damage. plainWeight/exoticWeight are the fallbacks; js/rpg.js AFFIX_WEIGHT names the ones worth steering.

world._doc: 256 x 128 cells at 640 m = a planet surface 163 km x 82 km.

terrain._viewDoc: maxViewScale caps how far the clipmap may be stretched. It is the player's View distance setting (0.5x-6x) multiplied by the flight stretch (up to 6x when you reach the ceiling), so the two compose and the ceiling has to clear 36.
terrain._doc: Concentric square rings centred on the player, each three times wider than the last at the same vertex count — near ground is 2 m per quad, the horizon 162 m. Five rings reach 7.8 km in five draw calls. ?quality=low uses the smaller set for headless tests. riverDepth is how deep a river cuts its valley into the ground, in metres.
terrain._roundDoc: The round-11 world fixes, all read by makeTerrain in js/planet.js. deckGrip: metres of abutment either side of a road where the graded deck keeps its ground after a river or lake is carved through it — this is what gives a bridge collision instead of letting you walk through it. mergeCells: how close two roads have to run, in map cells, before the lower-class one stops drawing a second line and joins the higher one at a junction (they used to weave). minLakeCells: a 'lake' smaller than this is the depression filler rounding one cell down, not water — it goes back to dry land on the map as well. roundLakeCells: a lake this size or smaller is drawn with a shoreline rather than as cell-sized squares with sharp corners.
terrain._reliefDoc: How tall the world is against how wide it is. universe/ gives a planet its TRUE relief — often 8 km — and this map is 90-160 km across, not 40,000, so the real number turns every coastline into a cliff. 0.22 keeps mountains that read as mountains and slopes you can walk up. It is multiplied by the planet-scale knob, so a smaller map gets proportionally smaller hills.

sky._doc: Real angular sizes make a sibling planet a single pixel, so siblings are drawn larger on purpose - the same cheat every space game makes. siblingScale 1 is the honest sky. Moons need no cheat: these worlds keep their moons 5-10 planet radii out (our own Moon is at 60), so moonScale 1 already fills a chunk of the sky. Sizes are computed from real orbital positions either way. startFraction is where in the day a new run begins: 0 midnight, 0.25 dawn, 0.5 noon. orbitScale/moonOrbitScale run the orbits on their own clock: at real speed a 365-day sibling needs ~91 hours of play to go round, so it looks welded to the sun.
sky._eclipseDoc: Seconds of run time before an eclipse may start. A day is 900 s, so 450 is two in-game hours: long enough that a new character's first impression of a sunlit world is a sunlit world.

props._doc: Scatter knobs. radius is in 64 m prop cells, so 7 is props out to ~450 m. density scales every kit; the debug menu changes it live.

features._doc: How far out rivers, roads, bridges and settlements are built, in metres.

weather._doc: How long a weather state holds and how long it takes to roll in. The states themselves and which ones a climate allows live in worldgen/js/weather.js.

save._doc: How often a run writes itself to browser storage. A save is the seed plus what the player did — never the world, which is a pure function of the seed.

space._doc: Space runs in its own compressed units: 1 AU is auUnits across and an Earth-sized planet is earthUnits in radius, because metres over a 163 km map and hundreds of millions of kilometres cannot share a coordinate space. speed is the cruise rate; boost and warp multiply it. landRange is how close to a world you must be, in its own radii, before you can put down. The approach knobs are a DISTANCE now, not body radii: slowWithinAu (0.1 AU) is where the throttle starts easing off toward slowTo, never wider than the lane a world owns so a compact system is not braked end to end, and never tighter than slowMinRadii of its own radii so the brake still bites on a small world. '26 body radii' was a third of an AU and stopped you boosting anywhere. noWarpWithinAu locks warp out near anything; exitMargin is how far outside the brake you surface when leaving atmosphere, so the planet does not simply catch you again; bodySpeed caps how fast any world may drift, as a share of cruise, because one orbitScale for every body had moons lapping in under a minute; and falling below entryAltitude over a landable world drops you into its atmosphere with no key press at all. warpSeconds is how long the jump between stars takes.

sound._doc: Which Sound Lab maker to use (synth, library, hybrid, retro) and the master volume. Audio starts on the first click, because a browser will not hand a page an audio context before that. ?sound=off turns both sound and voices off.

_retrainDoc: R20 — what an Unbinder charges. Forgetting a spell, a perk or a talent is the only way any of the three comes back now: the character sheet shows what you have taken and no longer takes it away again. `one` is the price at level 1 and `perLevel` is what each level past the first adds, so the cost keeps pace with the purse rather than becoming free. `all` / `allPerLevel` are the same two numbers for the wipe-the-lot button. Read by js/retrain.js; every number here is safe to tune without touching code.

town._doc: How close you must stand to talk to somebody, and how far from the player settlements keep their people.

ranks._doc: Every spawn rolls a rank. A champion takes one modifier and a rare takes two plus a name of its own, which is where 'go and kill the glowing one' comes from. Bosses are placed, never rolled.

zones._doc: Level bands come from the World Forge region graph: how many region borders from the one you started in. bandWidth is how many levels a single region spans. The starting region is always band 1 whatever the graph says.

chests._doc: Treasure on the ground. `perCell` is how many chests a 64 m prop cell may hold at density 1, which is deliberately tiny — finding one should be an event. Dungeons place their own on top of this. Every kind declares a `floor` rarity: the worst thing it may contain, and the colour of the beacon standing over it. The beam is a promise, so the two must never disagree — one shaft for a common find, four and a ring of motes for a legendary.

dungeon._doc: A dungeon is a real interior built from rooms and corridors, not a marker. `rooms` is how many the layout aims for at difficulty 1; deeper zones get more. Everything inside is dark, which is why a torch matters.

pets._doc: Companions. `perLevel` scales a pet off its OWNER's level so a pet never falls behind. It is 1.13 — the SAME number as `enemies.perLevel` — so a companion's share of a kill is the same at level 50 as at level 1. It was 1.17, which meant the share grew by (1.17/1.13)^(level-1): 2.1x by level 22 and 5.5x by 50. On top of that, js/followers.js caps a companion's damage at 75% of the top of the OWNER's own swing, because matching the exponents only stops the drift and the two curves were never related in the first place. `leash` is how far it may get from you before it gives up and comes back.

light._spotDoc: The ship's landing lights (B3). Two SpotLights either side of the centreline rather than one brighter lamp, because the value of a landing light is the CONE - you want the strip of ground you are about to put down on, not a uniform glow that washes the night out. `reach` is how far ahead the cones are aimed and `spread` how far apart the lamps sit.
light._doc: Night used to be unplayable. Every character now carries a torch; `torch` is its point light, `ambientNight` is the floor the sky light never drops below, and `maxLights` caps how many world lights (braziers, sconces, campfires) are switched on at once — the nearest win.
light._dungeonDoc: Underground, the same torch that throws a 20 m pool outdoors lit about four metres and you could not tell a doorway from a wall. The floor is high enough that geometry reads at about twelve metres; the dark comes from the COLOUR — a cold blue-grey — not from the player being unable to see.

encounters._doc: Set-piece encounters on the road, rolled instead of a plain pack. `everySeconds` is how often one is considered, `chance` how often the roll takes, and `maxLive` how many can be running at once. The weights are in data/encounters.json.
encounters._r21: R21: `radius` was 90, which put a whole set piece — including its buildings — between 49 and 99 m away. The play-test: "I just watched an entire building appear only ~100 meters away." 240 puts the ring at 132-240 m and the `ahead` case at 168-264 m, so a thing arrives on the horizon rather than in your lap. `ambushRadius` is deliberately NOT raised: an ambush is supposed to be on top of you. `keepRadius` is how far a set piece's own bodies survive, which HAS to be larger than the furthest a set piece can be placed — at the old 300 m despawn, an event placed at 264 m would have lost its guards almost immediately (see js/actors.js).

meteors._doc: A meteor is rolled every `everySeconds` on the surface and lands `fallSeconds` later, somewhere `landRange` metres away — far enough to be a walk, near enough to find. It is on the map and in the sky the whole time it is falling, and it leaves a Meteorite chest (see chests.kinds.meteorite): 1-3 items, never worse than rare, with the rarity beams. `shootingEvery` is the decorative streaks that never land.

flight._doc: Flying the ship inside the atmosphere. W and S are the throttle and the mouse steers, so the nose is where you are looking and the ship goes where the nose points. `liftMax` is how much of the ship's weight the wing carries at `liftSpeedFull`: at or above 1 the ship holds its altitude in level flight, which is what lets you cross a continent with one hand. `hoverFloor` is a soft floor over the terrain so looking at the scenery does not fly you into it - you can still dive into a hill deliberately. `ceiling` is where the air ends and js/space.js takes over.

_r18Mount: R18 — the gallop and the throw. Three mount affixes (`cond_mountStamina`, `cond_mountTrample`, `cond_mountCalm`) landed in derived fields nothing read, because the mechanics they describe did not exist. These are those mechanics' knobs: `gallopSeconds` is how long a mount can run flat out before dropping back (extended by mountStamina), `gallopBonus` how much faster that is, `gallopRecover` how fast it gets its wind back, and `mountThrowChance` the chance a hit while riding throws you (reduced by mountCalm).
